mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as capital costs fall and risk appetite rises.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >50% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decline and positive returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as recession fears dominate risk sentiment.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2 percentage points in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE rises >0.2pp in 1 month, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures exceeding 0.5% in one month signal robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as earnings growth accelerates.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in <50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise >0.5% in 1 month, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a monthly industrial production decline exceeding 0.5% signals manufacturing slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as profit margins contract.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >55% of instances when INDPRO declines >0.5% in 1 month during late-cycle expansion, or the effect size is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate increase exceeding 0.3% signals accelerating economic activity, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as corporate earnings momentum builds.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of periods when GDPC1 growth rises >0.3%, or the correlation between GDPC1 growth and returns is insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals rising inflation, prompting aggressive monetary tightening that causes negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3 percentage points in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises >0.3pp in 1 month, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deceleration in payroll growth (>0.2% decline) and rising unemployment (>0.1% increase) in one month indicate labor market contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate declines > 0.2% and UNRATE rises > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >55% of instances when PAYEMS growth declines >0.2% and UNRATE rises >0.1% in 1 month, or the interaction effect is insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a federal funds rate increase exceeding 0.25 percentage points over three months signals aggressive policy to curb inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25 percentage points in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises >0.25pp in 3 months during monetary tightening cycles, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
